text:
Your Switch games, running on your iPhone. 

 Not an emulator. No terminal. A macOS or Windows app does the whole build in a few clicks. 

 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

 🆕 Latest highlights

- Multi-engine workbench and Dark Glass UI : Switch in one click at the top of the Builds page or in Settings between nxnative , nxkit (Beta) (with Ed25519-verified self-updates and console overlay support via NXKIT OVERLAY ), and MacNativeGames (guarded for 5 maintained first-party Mac titles), all wrapped in the unified Dark Glass UI and redesigned two-column controller console mode.
- Hot-loaded iOS game frameworks, .p12 on-device signing, and slim shared IPA : All your games share a compact shell app of a few tens of megabytes ( DMMSLTR1 shader trailers move into external .img archives with foreground .nxpart auto-joining). Add or update games by hot-pushing or exporting DmGame.framework into Documents/Frameworks without reinstalling the shell IPA (sideload users can import a .p12 certificate in the iOS app for automatic on-device signing), in 10 UI languages .
- Persistent build seeds and fast batch refresh : Builds made with 1.5 persist build-seeds , so most subsequent engine upgrades finish in minutes via batch refresh without keeping the original game package or build folders, paired with per-game update version badges (such as 1.5 ) and three-way missing .img recovery. The Windows launcher ( NX2Apple-windows-x64.zip ) also adds a general multi-game BuildQueue , an emulated heap growing up to 2 GiB on demand, and in-app self-update ( NX2Apple.exe ).
- Shortcuts with PiP guide, audio mixing, and controllers : iPhone and iPad add a built-in 6-step Add to Home Screen wizard with an optional Picture-in-Picture walkthrough card and controller-connect auto-launch, background audio mixing ( DM AUDIO MIX ), an interactive 16:9 cover cropper, a visual touch layout editor, split Bluetooth Joy-Con sideways mapping on Mac, and Steam Controller (2026) support.
- 208 game profiles, including 19 Switch 2 games : Pick a Switch 2 game folder or .nup file in the Mac or Windows launcher with no prod.keys needed, backed by Nintendo eShop banner fallback across Mac, iOS, and Windows.

Every release is in the changelog.

 

---

 What NX2Apple is

NX2Apple runs Nintendo Switch games on your Mac and iPhone from your own game dumps. It is not an
emulator: the game's own code runs natively on Apple silicon, and Metal draws it. A Mac app, the
launcher, does the build in a few clicks (unpack, rewrite, translate the shaders, pack) and then
keeps your games in a library you start with Play , the way a Switch does.

 

It is a community fork of nxnative , which does the actual
work (the code rewriter, the Horizon host, NVN on Metal and every game's profile). This fork adds the
launcher and a short list of patches, and follows nxnative every day.

 Requirements

- An Apple silicon Mac. The launcher opens on macOS 13 or later . Building needs Xcode with
 the iOS SDK, and NVN games need Xcode 27.2 (macOS 26.6
 or later) unless built with --allow-other-metal . Take 27.2 from Apple's download page, not the App Store's newer
 Xcode. With both installed, give 27.2 a distinct name such as Xcode-27.2.app . In Settings →
 Tools → Choose Xcode… , select the copy to use with NX2Apple, including one on an external
 drive. During first-run setup, click Set up later to reach Settings, then Run setup again 
 after choosing Xcode. Use system Xcode follows the Mac's command-line selection (for example,
 sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode-27.2.app ).
- Your own game dumps (NSP or XCI) and your own prod.keys from your own console. Nothing is
 bundled, downloaded or looked up for you. The same prod.keys opens every one of your Switch
 games. A current dump covers all retail titles. Switch 2 games (a game folder or .nup file) do not need
 prod.keys .
- For an iPhone or iPad: iOS or iPadOS 26 or later and a recent device. Older devices are untested.

The app carries its own build tools and Python, so no Homebrew and no Python install are needed. The
default nxnative engine still lets the app install the .NET SDK 10 for you in one click, while the
native nxkit engine needs neither Python nor .NET. The launcher's dependency page checks each
requirement and installs what it can with one click.

 Install

1. Download the app : NX2Apple-macOS-arm64.zip from the
 latest release. Unzip it.
2. Open it once with right-click, then Open. The app is not signed with a paid Apple developer
 certificate, so macOS asks before the first start. After that it opens normally.
3. Follow the setup. The launcher fetches the project it builds with (a Download repository 
 button on the setup page, a shallow clone into /NX2Apple . If GitHub is slow, the page shows the
 manual ZIP route), checks the tools above and updates itself later. You never need git.
4. Build a game. Pick the game's folder (or its base game, update, DLC and prod.keys one by
 one), choose This Mac or iPhone / iPad , and press build. The page shows the real stages and
 the time left, and a stopped build continues where it left off. The iPhone / iPad target is one
 app on the device for all your games. The launcher signs it with Xcode, installs it and copies the
 game in. It needs a device paired with the Mac.

Building by hand from a terminal is in BUILDING.md.

install.title: Install
install.html:
1. Download the app: NX2Apple-macOS-arm64.zip from the latest release. Unzip it.
  2. Open it once with right-click, then Open. The app is not signed with a paid Apple developer certificate, so macOS asks before the first start. After that it opens normally.
  3. Follow the setup. The launcher fetches the project it builds with (a Download repository button on the setup page, a shallow clone into ~/NX2Apple. If GitHub is slow, the page shows the manual ZIP route), checks the tools above and updates itself later. You never need git.
  4. Build a game. Pick the game's folder (or its base game, update, DLC and prod.keys one by one), choose This Mac or iPhone / iPad, and press build. The page shows the real stages and the time left, and a stopped build continues where it left off. The iPhone / iPad target is one app on the device for all your games. The launcher signs it with Xcode, installs it and copies the game in. It needs a device paired with the Mac.

Building by hand from a terminal is in BUILDING.md.

Updating a game you already built. Games built with 1.5 persist local build seeds, so when syncing engine improvements you can use Refresh or Batch refresh to update in minutes without keeping the original NSP/XCI or _build folders. When installing a newer update NSP for the game itself, select the game in the library and choose Rebuild, keeping the base game selected and picking the new NSP in Updates & add-on content in the same output folder. The update can change both game code and data, so the launcher builds the new version and reuses cached work where it can. Your saves stay in their existing folder outside the .app, keyed by the game's title ID. Rebuilding or refreshing in the same library keeps that progress.
